claimed_purpose.text: Manages memory across three tiers: short-term, mid-term, and long-term, with an Updater class coordinating promotion and analysis-driven writes.
Hierarchical storage with four core modules: Storage, Updating, Retrieval, and Generation for comprehensive memory management

mechanisms.text: Four core modules: Storage, Updating, Retrieval, and Generation
Memory is isolated per user and per assistant via user_id and assistant_id at initialization

Three distinct stores are persisted: user_profiles (per-user profile strings with timestamps), knowledge_base (user private knowledge entries), and assistant_knowledge (assistant-specific knowledge entries). All are serialized to a JSON file on every write.
Knowledge entries are curated facts, not raw message logs. Each entry stores the knowledge text, a timestamp, and a precomputed normalized embedding vector.
User profile update supports merge (appends new data to existing string with a dated separator) or overwrite (replace=False), with last_updated timestamp recorded.
Three-tier memory architecture: short-term, mid-term, and long-term, each backed by separate JSON files per user.
When short-term memory is full, its contents are migrated to mid-term memory before the new entry is added.
Isolation is per user_id and per assistant_id: user data and assistant knowledge live in separate directory trees.
Persists session objects (summary, detail pages, embeddings, heat score, visit counts, timestamps) to a JSON file on disk via json.dump.
A continuity check gate determines whether a new conversation page is a true continuation of the previous one or a topic shift — controls whether new content is appended to an existing memory unit.

Personality analysis extracts user traits across 90 named dimensions (psychological, AI-alignment, interest/content) and updates the persistent user profile; dimensions absent from both old profile and new conversation are omitted — an implicit delete-by-omission on stale inferences.
Three-tier memory store: short-term, mid-term, and long-term layers implemented as separate modules
Memory is added as user_input and assistant_response pairs, suggesting a log-style write path capturing conversation turns.
A separate user profile store captures personality traits, preferences, and related knowledge — distinct from raw memory entries.
When short-term memory reaches capacity, it triggers promotion to mid-term memory.
The questioner speculates the list type on evicted_qas may be defensive coding for edge cases rather than a functional requirement.
Mid-term memory (MTM) is organized into sessions containing pages; a summary_embedding field represents the semantic content of a session.
MemoryOS uses two separate LongTermMemory instances — one for the assistant and one for the user — despite LongTermMemory already having attributes for both user and assistant.
The proposed storage provider interface covers add, update, delete, search, and metadata handling
Three-tier hierarchical memory store: short-term QA pairs, mid-term topic-based segments with heat tracking, long-term user profile and knowledge
add_memory API: persists a user_input / agent_response QA pair with optional timestamp and metadata

ledger.claim: Hierarchical three-tier memory architecture (short-term, mid-term, long-term) inspired by OS memory management
ledger.quote: Drawing inspiration from memory management principles in operating systems, it adopts a hierarchical storage architecture with four core modules: Storage, Updating, Retrieval, and Generation, to achieve comprehensive and efficient memory management.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Mid-term segments are promoted to long-term when heat exceeds threshold; user profile and knowledge are updated via LLM analysis
ledger.quote: Mid-term memory segments accumulate "heat" based on factors like visit frequency and interaction length. When a segment's heat exceeds a threshold, its content is analyzed: User profile insights are extracted and used to update the long-term user profile. Specific user facts are added to the user's long-term knowledge.
ledger.label: measured

unknowns.text: Forget / delete: no mechanism described for deleting specific memories or removing entries from any tier's store
Conflict / supersession: no description of how contradictory facts in long-term knowledge are reconciled or overwritten

Isolation scope: no prompt here addresses whether memory is per-user, per-session, per-agent, or per-character. The {relationship} role slot hints at character-level isolation but the store scoping is not stated.
Isolation scope is not explicit here: user_id is passed to long-term profile writes but it is unclear whether mid-term pages are also scoped per user or are shared across users/sessions.
Forget / delete path: the page describes add_memory, retrieve_memory, and get_user_profile but does not document any API or mechanism for deleting or expiring stored memories
Conflict and supersession: no description of how contradictory or outdated facts in long-term or mid-term store are resolved or overwritten
Retrieve policy: no description of when retrieval is skipped or whether retrieval is always performed on every turn
No forget or delete mechanism is described or listed as a tool on this page; unclear whether deletion from store is supported.
Retrieval policy (always retrieve vs. adaptive/conditional) is not described; only that retrieval is query-driven.

The page does not describe what process_short_term_to_mid_term does with the evicted QA pairs after collecting them in evicted_qas — how or whether they are written into mid-term storage is not shown.
The page does not describe the retrieve policy: how memories are selected from short-term, mid-term, or long-term stores into a turn's context.
No maintainer response is present in the extracted page text explaining the intended design of evicted_qas as a list in updater.py.
Overall end-to-end compute cost comparison across all memory pipeline steps is absent from the evaluation; issue explicitly asks whether this data exists
Whether per-call user_id on add_memory (or other write/read operations) is planned or supported; the issue is a feature request with no maintainer response visible on this page
No response or maintainer explanation is present in the extracted text; the rationale for dual LongTermMemory instantiation (isolation design choice vs. bug) is unresolved on this page.
The README's stated pluggable storage engine design is referenced but not quoted or described in this issue; the gap between documented design and actual implementation is unresolved here.
Explicit forget/delete API: this blog describes eviction via FIFO and heat decay but does not describe a user-facing delete or forget call

No description of how conflicting or contradictory facts in User KB are resolved during incremental updates — the LPM update section states extraction and update occur but does not specify supersession or conflict handling policy.

No description of explicit delete or forget operation on LPM entries — only MTM eviction and FIFO overflow for User KB/Agent Traits queues are described; whether users or agents can explicitly remove memories is not addressed.
